scale: 1 = not at all true, 3 = partly true, 5 = fully true and measured

questions.text: Leadership has named 2-3 business outcomes AI should improve this year, with targets and an owner.
There is a budget and a named owner for AI initiatives.
Core data (customers, jobs, tickets, invoices) lives in systems we can export or query — not in personal spreadsheets.
Data quality is known and someone is accountable for it.
Every employee has an approved, enterprise-grade AI assistant (for example Gemini in Google Workspace).
Our main systems have APIs or connectors we can automate against.
Most employees have had basic training on using AI safely and well.
At least one person can build, test and evaluate AI workflows.
We have a written AI use policy (which data may be used, which tools are approved, what needs review).
AI outputs that reach customers are reviewed by a human or systematically tested.
Teams share AI tips and wins openly and experimentation is encouraged.
Managers have redesigned at least one process around AI instead of bolting it on.

levels.name: Exploring
levels.description: Curiosity and individual experiments; no shared direction.

levels.name: Experimenting
levels.description: Pockets of use with approved tools; no policy, metrics or owner.

levels.name: Formalising
levels.description: Policy, owner and first measured use cases; data gaps known.

levels.name: Scaling
levels.description: Several use cases in production with KPIs; reusable patterns and training.

levels.name: Transforming
levels.description: Processes redesigned around AI; continuous evaluation and improvement.

strategy: Name an executive owner and 3 measurable AI outcomes for the next 2 quarters
Ring-fence a small AI budget (1-2% of opex) with a quarterly review
data: Name a data owner per core entity (customer, job, invoice) and publish a data-quality scorecard
Move critical spreadsheets into the system of record or BigQuery
tools: Roll out the approved assistant to every role with role-specific prompts
List the APIs/connectors of the top 5 systems and their owners
skills: Run a 90-minute 'AI at work' session for everyone and a deeper track for 2-3 builders
Create a prompt library per department
governance: Publish a one-page AI use policy (approved tools, data classes, human review)
Add an AI section to the security review and vendor checklist
culture: Start a monthly 'AI show-and-tell' and a shared wins channel
Ask each manager to redesign one process end to end
